items.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Eric Leinsdorf, who became the conductor of the Boston Symphony, and who admired my work and recorded one of my most famous pieces with the Boston Symphony... he hired me to become, in effect, the artistic director of the school of Tanglewood.

ctx.x: Yeah. That’s right. It was down to 215. People had – people were not coming to the Conservatory. Couldn’t get any students. It’s reputation was just about finished. Financially – I found out later that there were only something like $200,000 left in the till, or some terrible small amount. You couldn’t run a conservatory for more than three weeks that way. I was so innocent. I’m a high-school dropout. First of all, I didn’t even know the difference between a graduate degree and undergraduate degree. These were…
You thought about starting a jazz department.
